name: Vyravid
verdictSummary: A local version of Vyravid around the core workflow: project dashboard, script-to-scenes generation, voiceover generation, media generation, timeline assembly, and local ffmpeg rendering. The hard parts are not the CRUD shell but the many media edge cases, provider integrations, long-running jobs, and polished editor behavior.
coreLoopDIY: Create a local project, generate or paste a script, generate voiceover, split the script into scenes, create visual prompts/assets, arrange a timeline, apply simple effects, and render the final video locally.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for hosted services, managed storage, fewer setup steps, reliable provider orchestration, templates, collaboration, asset libraries, support, and polished timeline UX. A local open-source rebuild can replace the workflow for technical users, but hosted products still win on convenience and reliability.
prompt: Build me a standalone local AI-assisted video generator. Use a Vue 3 frontend with Vite, Pinia, Vue Router, and a FastAPI backend. Use SQLite for the database and local filesystem storage for media. Create a dashboard at /app that shows local project stats and recent projects. Create a projects page at /app/projects that lists existing projects from SQLite with search/filter behavior. Create a project editor at /app/projects/:id for building a video from script, scenes, generated media, voiceover, and timeline settings. Use a fixed local user ID for all local data. Store projects in data/db/vyravid.sqlite3 and media under data/storage, served from /media. Keep project IDs stable when editing existing projects. Implement a FastAPI backend on port 8000 with routers for projects, dashboard stats, image generation, audio/TTS generation, scene generation, scene storage, characters, music, and video processing. Mount an embedded video processor under /vp/* in the same FastAPI process. Implement a local SQLite so service and repository code can call table(...).select(...).eq(...).insert(...).update(...).delete(...).execute(). Implement local storage helpers store files locally and return http://localhost:8000/media/... URLs. Support project creation, draft saving, project details loading, scene saving/loading, text layers, timeline backgrounds, generated image records, audio records, custom voices, and project languages. For AI providers, support bring-your-own API keys through .env. Include Google Gemini for text/image-related generation, MiniMax or Google TTS for voiceover, Replicate for optional image/video provider calls, and faster-whisper for local transcription. Make provider failures visible but do not break local project browsing. Use ffmpeg for local video assembly, captions, audio/video synchronization, image timelines, transitions, green screen overlays, Ken Burns-style movement, and final video rendering. Expose video rendering endpoints through /vp and call them from the main backend. The backend script should load .env or app/.env, then derive local paths from the checkout directory: VYRAVID_ROOT, VYRAVID_DATA, VYRAVID_DB, DATABASE_URL, VYRAVID_PUBLIC_BASE. The frontend script should set VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 and run Vite on port 5173. Create .env.example with local defaults and empty provider keys. Design the frontend as a real video creation workspace. The first screen after /app should be the dashboard. Use practical dense UI for projects, scenes, media, timeline controls, voice settings, and rendering status. Include loading, error, empty, and completed states. Add README setup instructions, local data paths, active ports, environment behavior, database inspection commands, and build/type-check commands. Keep the app runnable locally with SQLite and filesystem media storage.
